title: Automate weekly train: RC orchestration, LTS demarcation, and release-notes synthesis
creator: Lena Chen
description: Goal: Replace the manual weekly cut checklist with an automated pipeline that creates RC tags, synthesizes release notes from merged PR metadata, applies LTS demarcation rules, and triggers gated rollouts. This ticket covers the orchestration layer (GitHub Actions + internal runner), policy decisions for versioning and LTS marking, and integration points with the upgrade CLI and Console rollout controller.
acceptance_criteria: A1: GitHub Actions workflow 'weekly-cut-orchestrator' runs on schedule and creates a reproducible RC tag format (rc/<major>.<minor>-YYYYMMDD-<train-id>)
A2: Release notes draft is auto-generated from PR labels (breaking/feature/fix), PR descriptions, and linked issues; maintainer can edit a short summary before publishing
A3: LTS eligible minor releases are flagged via manifest rule and an LTS tag (lts/<major>.<minor>) is created only when automated SLO gates pass
A4: The orchestrator invokes a smoke-test suite and SLO checks; failures prevent RC promotion and post a detailed failure summary to the release channel
A5: Upgrade CLI 'redwood-upgrade' is notified with a new upgrade plan artifact (JSON) and validates migration steps for consumers
A6: Rollout controller receives rollout policy and can apply a canary percentage; rollback hooks are wired to the RC tag
A7: Production run of the pipeline recorded in the release dashboard and linked in the release notes
implementation_steps: Design RC tag format and document versioning rules in Confluence (doc link below)
Author GitHub Actions workflow 'weekly-cut-orchestrator' that: checks branch hygiene, computes version bump, creates RC tag, and opens a Draft GitHub Release
Implement release-notes-generator lambda that collects merged PRs since last tag, groups by label, and creates a markdown draft with auto-summary and manual edit endpoint
Add manifest rule engine to mark LTS candidates based on Minor release parity and ops approval signal
Wire the orchestration to call the SLO + smoke test APIs and enforce gating; publish gate results to Slack and release channel
Emit upgrade plan artifact and upload to release artifacts store; call 'redwood-upgrade validate' as a post-cut check
Add docs and runbook: rollback steps, emergency hotfix process, and how to manually re-run the orchestrator

notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: Use label-driven release notes vs. semantic commit messages. Label approach is friendlier to current process but requires stricter PR hygiene enforcement.
Decision: RC tag format will include a date and train-id to avoid collisions in back-to-back cuts (rc/1.22-20260314-w11).

Trade-off: Automated LTS promotion reduces manual ops work but increases blast-radius if gating is misconfigured; we require manual approval step for first two LTS promotions after rollout automation is enabled.
Fallback: If the orchestrator fails, we keep the existing manual checklist as a hot path and provide a 'manual cut' CLI that runs the same steps with operator input.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for release-notes-generator (label parsing, PR deduping) - coverage target 90%
End-to-end test of Actions workflow in staging repo that mimics production merges and verifies a Draft Release is created
Chaos test: simulate SLO API timeout and ensure orchestrator reports failure and does not promote RC
Integration test: 'redwood-upgrade validate' runs against the upgrade artifact and reports compatibility matrix
rollback_plan: If RC promotes with regressions detected, trigger automatic rollback using release-controller rollback API
Recreate last stable tag and re-run canary rollout with 0% -> 50% -> 100% progression after fixes
Notify customers via status page and attach hotfix backlog items to the release notes
